callPoints.title: 컨퍼런스콜 핵심
callPoints.speaker: Bill McDermott, CEO; Gina Mastantuono, 사장 겸 CFO

points.text: AI 수요가 예상보다 강해 AI 신규 ACV 기대치를 웃돌았고, 2026년 AI ACV 목표를 연초 10억 달러에서 17억 달러로 상향했다고 CFO가 설명했다.
경영진은 생산 환경의 에이전틱 AI 사용량이 연초 이후 전년 대비 13배 이상 늘었고, Q3에 500만 달러 초과 신규 ACV 계약 19건을 체결했다고 밝혔다.
투자·효율 측면에서 자본지출을 줄이는 자본효율적 모델을 강조하며, 연간 잉여현금흐름 마진 목표를 100bp 높여 36%로 제시했다.
가이던스 설명에서 회사는 2026년 비GAAP 영업이익률 31.5%, 구독 총이익률 81%를 제시했고, CEO는 AI·보안·기술부채를 통합 관리하는 ‘Control Tower’ 전략이 고객의 채택을 가속한다고 강조했다.
공개된 회사 실적자료에는 컨퍼런스콜 질의응답의 구체적 문답이 확인되지 않아 Q&A 쟁점은 자료만으로 요약하지 않았다.

dropped.text: Q3 구독 매출은 39억8,800만 달러로 전년 대비 21% 늘었고, 비GAAP 영업이익률은 32.5%였다. 회사는 연간 구독 매출 가이던스를 157억8,000만~157억9,000만 달러로 제시했다.

briefs.headline: 연준, 정책금리 범위 유지

figures.label: 정책금리 범위
figures.quote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.

figures.label: 표결
figures.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10 - 2 vote:

details.label: 경제활동
details.quote: Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace.

details.label: 물가 목표 복귀
details.text: 추가 정보가 적절한 정책 기조 결정에 도움이 될 것이라고 밝혔다.
details.quote: The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal.

details.label: 정책 조치
details.text: 직전 성명의 금리 인상 문구를 금리 범위 유지 문구로 바꿨다.
details.quote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.

dissents.label: Lisa D. Cook, Beth M. Hammack
dissents.text: 두 위원은 이번 회의에서 금리 범위 인상을 선호했다.
dissents.quote: Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

watch: 다음 FOMC 성명과 정책 기조를 확인한다.
물가와 고용 지표를 살핀다.
추가 정보가 정책 판단에 미치는 영향을 확인한다.

points.text: 고용 여건은 긍정적이지만 물가는 여전히 목표를 웃돈다고 평가했다. “So on the employment side of the Feds dual mandate, conditions are quite positive.” “But inflation is too high.”

에너지·관련 가격 상승이 다른 부문으로 확산되지 않고 기대인플레이션이 안정적으로 유지되도록 하는 것이 과제라고 밝혔다. “And our job is to ensure that relative price changes in some sectors do not broaden out across the economy, and that inflation expectations remain as they are anchored.”

금융 여건은 긴축됐지만 이를 긴축적이라고 단정하지 않았으며, 향후 정보에 따라 적절한 정책 수준을 판단하겠다고 말했다. “And while overall financial conditions are tighter, Im unwilling and unable to call them tight.” “The information we receive over the coming period will help us determine where we want policy to be.”
제공된 발췌문에는 대차대조표에 관한 발언이나 기자 질문과 답변이 포함되어 있지 않다. “Now my time is yours, and I welcome your questions.”

points.text: 수요: 경영진은 AI 인프라 투자가 클라우드 매출과 고객사의 실적에 반영되고 있다고 설명하고, HBM4 출하량·매출이 4분기에 HBM3E를 넘어설 것으로 내다봤다.
질의응답 쟁점—AI 수요 지속성: 경영진은 주요 고객의 클라우드 성장, 수주 잔고와 AI 서비스 유료 이용 증가를 근거로 수요가 견조하다고 설명했다.

dropped.text: 투자·가시성: 2027~2028년 생산능력의 절반 이상을 장기공급계약으로 확보했으며, 내년 투자를 크게 늘리되 고객 수요·수익성·투자 효율을 따져 규모와 시기를 조정하겠다고 밝혔다.
마진: 3분기 영업이익률은 80%였으며, 회사는 시장 상황을 반영하는 장기계약 가격 구조로 안정적인 수익성을 확보하겠다고 설명했다.
가이던스 설명: M15X를 연말까지 최대 가동하고, 4분기 HBM4를 주력 제품으로 확대하는 한편 내년 매출과 이익을 한 단계 더 키우겠다는 계획을 제시했다.

briefs.checkText: Document Meta Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Announces Establishment of New Class C Common Stock MENLO PARK, Calif. - October 21, 2026 - Meta Platforms, Inc. (Nasdaq: META) today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. "We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model," said Mark Zuckerberg, Meta founder and CEO. "Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we're seeing velocity across the board." Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights Three Months Ended September 30, % Change In millions, except percentages and per share amounts 2026 2025 Revenue $ 64,601 $ 51,242 26 % Costs and expenses 51,613 30,707 68 % Income from operations $ 12,988 $ 20,535 (37) % Operating margin 20 % 40 % Provision for income taxes $ 3,141 $ 18,954 (83) % Effective tax rate 24 % 87 % Net income $ 9,860 $ 2,709 264 % Diluted earnings per share (EPS) $ 3.83 $ 1.05 265 % Agreement with U.S. State Attorneys General In August 2026, we announced an agreement with 52 attorneys general to resolve litigation related to teen mental health and social media, which provides for payments of up to approximately $18.59 billion. Third quarter 2026 costs and expenses includes a $9.89 billion charge related to this agreement. Excluding this charge, the third quarter 2026: • Income from operations of $12.99 billion would have increased by $9.89 billion to $22.88 billion. • Diluted EPS of $3.83 would have increased by $3.57 to $7.40. • Effective tax rate of 24% would have decreased by 7 percentage points to 17%. Third Quarter 2026 Operational and Other Financial Highlights • Family daily active people (DAP) - DAP was 3.64 billion on average for September 2026, an increase of 3% year-over-year. • Ad impressions - Ad impressions delivered across our Family of Apps increased by 10% year-over-year. • Average price per ad - Average price per ad increased by 14% year-over-year. • Revenue - Revenue was $64.60 billion, an increase of 26% year-over-year on both a reported and constant currency basis. • Costs and expenses - Total costs and expenses were $51.61 billion, an increase of 68% year-over-year. This includes the litigation charge as discussed above. • Capital expenditures - Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $34.91 billion. • Capital return program - Dividend and dividend equivalent payments were $1.36 billion. • Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities - Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $82.45 billion as of September 30, 2026. • Cash flow - Cash flow from operating activities was $32.79 billion, and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. (1) • Headcount - Headcount was 66,775 as of September 30, 2026, a decrease of 15% year-over-year. ____________________________________ (1) For more information on our free cash flow non-GAAP financial measure, see the sections entitled "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and "Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Results" in this press release. 1 CFO Outlook Commentary We expect fourth quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $73-76 billion. Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates. We are raising our expense outlook to incorporate the $9.9 billion charge related to legal proceedings recognized in the third quarter. We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175-179 billion. Excluding the third quarter legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income. At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion. We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $135-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $130-145 billion. Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our fourth quarter 2026 tax rate to be between 15-17%. Additionally, we continue to monitor active legal and regulatory matters that could significantly impact our business and financial results. For example, we continue to see scrutiny on youth-related issues in several markets and have a number of youth-related trials scheduled in the coming months in the U.S. Looking beyond 2026, we are still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year, but we expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives. Our current capacity and what is scheduled to come online gives us the flexibility to allocate resources across model training, core business growth, and the development and support of new products. Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization. Building on this progress, our MSL investments are creating the technology and infrastructure needed to unlock significant new revenue opportunities and strengthen capabilities across the business. While these investments will take longer to generate returns than those in our core business, the breadth of monetization opportunities and internal efficiencies gives us confidence in their long-term potential. Looking ahead, although we are not providing a full-year 2027 revenue outlook, the benefits our AI investments are delivering to the core business, combined with emerging opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027. Separately, we remain focused on improving Reality Labs profitability and expect losses to narrow next year to around $15 billion as we reallocate investment toward other priority areas, primarily AI. 2 Establishment of New Class C Common Stock The Board of Directors has approved the establishment of a new class of publicly listed, non-voting Class C common stock, with an effective date in January 2027. The approval by Meta's Board follows the unanimous recommendation of a Special Committee of disinterested and independent directors, which was established by the Board to evaluate the company's capital structure. The Special Committee and the Board determined that creating this new class of stock is advisable, fair, and in the best interests of Meta and its shareholders for a number of reasons, including: • Creating a New Class of Shares for Capital Raising, Employee Compensation, Potential Acquisitions, and Other General Corporate Purposes - The scale of investment required to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives amidst the AI transformation taking place in the industry is significant. The Special Committee determined this new class of common stock will provide Meta the ability to finance its growth and help the company remain a leader among fierce competition both domestic and international. • Continuing to Maximize Long-Term Value for All Shareholders - Since Meta's formation, its management team has prioritized long-term goals and value creation, and its stock price has increased by more than 1,700% since its IPO. By contrast, over the same period, the S&P 500 has increased approximately 495%. The Special Committee wants Meta to continue innovating with an emphasis on long-term growth, which the creation of the Class C stock is intended to help facilitate. • Ensuring Founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg Continues to Lead Meta into the Next Era - The Special Committee concluded that Mr. Zuckerberg is best suited to lead Meta into its next era and beyond. They recognized that Meta's track record of significant value creation for its shareholders is in large part due to his strong leadership, unique and creative vision, and exceptional management abilities. The creation of the Class C common stock will continue the founder-led model that has driven the company's success since its inception. Meta intends to file an amended and restated certificate of incorporation in Delaware to establish the Class C common stock, with an effective date of January 19, 2027. The Board has also declared a one-time stock dividend of one share of Class C common stock for each outstanding share of Class A common stock and Class B common stock, contingent upon, and to be paid after, the effectiveness of the amended and restated certificate of incorporation. The record date and payment date of the stock dividend will be determined by the Board at a later date. After the payment date of the stock dividend, we expect the market price for our Class A common stock to reflect the effect of a two-for-one stock split. The stock dividend will not change the voting power of any shareholder. The amended and restated certificate of incorporation has been approved by shareholder written consent. We have also entered into a Founder Alignment Agreement with Mr. Zuckerberg, which has terms related to his sales of Class C common stock received in the stock dividend, his service at the company, and conditions for potential future stock dividends of Class C common stock. Meta's Class A common stock will continue to trade on Nasdaq, and we intend to qualify the Class C common stock for listing on Nasdaq upon its issuance as a result of the stock dividend. More information will be available in our Report on Form 8-K and information statement to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Moelis & Company LLC served as independent financial advisor to the Special Committee and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC served as financial advisor to Meta. 3 Webcast and Conference Call Information Meta will host a conference call to discuss its results at 1:30 p.m. PT / 4:30 p.m. ET today. The live webcast of the call can be accessed at the Meta Investor Relations website at investor.atmeta.com, along with the company's earnings press release, financial tables, and slide presentation. Following the call, a replay will be available at the same website. Transcripts of conference calls with publishing equity research analysts held today will also be posted to the investor.atmeta.com website. Disclosure Information Meta uses the investor.atmeta.com and meta.com/news websites as well as Mark Zuckerberg's Facebook profile (facebook.com/zuck), Instagram account (instagram.com/zuck) and Threads profile (threads.net/zuck) as means of disclosing material non-public information and for complying with its disclosure obligations under Regulation FD. About Meta Meta is building the future of human connection, powered by artificial intelligence and immersive technologies. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram, and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving toward building experiences that foster deeper connections and unlock new possibilities. Contacts Investors: Rob Bevegni investor@meta.com / investor.atmeta.com Press: Matt Tye press@meta.com / meta.com/news 4 Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements regarding our future business plans and expectations. These forward-looking statements are only predictions and may differ materially from actual results due to a variety of factors including: the impact of macroeconomic conditions on our business and financial results, including as a result of geopolitical events; our ability to retain or increase users and engagement levels; our reliance on advertising revenue; our dependency on data signals and mobile operating systems, networks, and standards that we do not control; changes to the content or application of third-party policies that impact our advertising practices; risks associated with new products and changes to existing products as well as other new business initiatives, including our artificial intelligence initiatives and Reality Labs efforts; our emphasis on community growth and engagement and the user experience over short-term financial results; maintaining and enhancing our brand and reputation; our ongoing privacy, safety, security, and content and advertising review and enforcement efforts; competition; risks associated with government actions that could restrict access to our products or impair our ability to sell advertising in certain countries; litigation and government inquiries; privacy, legislative, and regulatory concerns or developments; risks associated with acquisitions; security breaches; our ability to manage our scale and geographically-dispersed operations; and market conditions or other factors affecting capital return to stockholders. These and other potential risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ from the results predicted are more fully detailed under the caption "Risk Factors" in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q filed with the SEC on July 30, 2026, which is available on our Investor Relations website at investor.atmeta.com and on the SEC website at www.sec.gov. Additional information will also be set forth in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. In addition, please note that the date of this press release is October 21, 2026, and any forward-looking statements contained herein are based on assumptions that we believe to be reasonable as of this date. We undertake no obligation to update these statements as a result of new information or future events. For a discussion of limitations in the measurement of certain of our community metrics, see the section entitled "Limitations of Key Metrics and Other Data" in our most recent quarterly or annual report filed with the SEC. Non-GAAP Financial Measures To supplement our condensed consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (GAAP), we use the following non-GAAP financial measures: revenue excluding foreign exchange effect, advertising revenue excluding foreign exchange effect, and free cash flow. The presentation of these financial measures is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, financial information prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP. Investors are cautioned that there are material limitations associated with the use of non-GAAP financial measures as an analytical tool. In addition, these measures may be different from non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies, limiting their usefulness for comparison purposes. We compensate for these limitations by providing specific information regarding the GAAP amounts excluded from these non-GAAP financial measures. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures provide investors with useful supplemental information about the financial performance of our business, enable comparison of financial results between periods where certain items may vary independent of business performance, and allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in operating our business. Our non-GAAP financial measures are adjusted for the following items: Foreign exchange effect on revenue . To calculate revenue on a constant currency basis, we translate current period revenue using the prior year's monthly exchange rates for our settlement or billing currencies other than the U.S. dollar, which we believe is a useful metric that facilitates comparison to our historical performance. Purchases of property and equipment; Principal payments on finance leases. We subtract both purchases of property and equipment, and principal payments on finance leases in our calculation of free cash flow because we believe that these two items collectively represent the amount of property and equipment we need to procure to support our business, regardless of whether we procure such property or equipment with a finance lease. We believe that this methodology can provide useful supplemental information to help investors better understand underlying trends in our business. Free cash flow is not intended to represent our residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures. For more information on our non-GAAP financial measures and a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP measures, see the "Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Results" table in this press release. 5 META PLATFORMS, INC.
